Oil rebounds after Trump rejects Iran peace deal

SINGAPORE, Sept 28 (Reuters) - Oil prices rebounded more than 1% on Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude futures rose $1.82, or 1.74%, to $106.14 a barrel by 2202 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $93.55 a barrel, up $1.14, or 1.23%.

(Reporting by Florence Tan)

--- SECOND REUTERS WIRE, same story, later Asian-session snapshot ---
URL: https://www.asiaone.com/money/oil-rebounds-after-trump-rejects-iran-peace-deal
AsiaOne carrying Reuters, published 28 September 2026 1:51 AM (SGT). In-text: "Monday (Sept 28)".

SINGAPORE - Oil prices rebounded more than one per cent on Monday (Sept 28) after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, keeping tensions in the Middle East elevated.

Brent crude futures rose US$1.32, or 1.27 per cent, to US$105.64 a barrel by 12.36am GMT (8.36 am SGT) while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$93.11 a barrel, up 70 cents, or 0.76 per cent.

Iran announced a peace proposal last week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators. Trump said on Saturday he rejected the plan, but told Axios in a phone interview on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in more talks this week.

--- THIRD REUTERS WIRE: equities/bonds, Monday Asian session ---
URL: https://www.asiaone.com/money/stocks-cautious-asia-oil-gains-yields-rise
AsiaOne carrying Reuters (Wayne Cole, Sydney), published 28 September 2026. In-text "Monday (Sept 28)".

SYDNEY - Share markets made a cautious start on Monday (Sept 28) as oil prices popped higher again amid doubts the US and Iran will reach a truce anytime soon, keeping bonds under pressure ahead of a week packed with economic news.

Over the weekend, US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming Tehran was desperate to make a deal. Trump said talks would continue this week, though Iran shows no sign of watering down its proposals.

Brent futures quickly rose 1.6 per cent to US$106.00 a barrel, bringing gains so far this month to 17 per cent, while US crude futures added 1.1 per cent to US$93.47 a barrel.

Japan's Nikkei gained 0.8 per cent, while South Korean stocks dipped 0.6 per cent. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.2 per cent.

Yields on [1]0-year Treasuries nudged up to 5.51[5] per cent [...] 7 basis points [...] yields have shot up 55 basis points this month in anticipation of Fed hikes.
